lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 3 you met characters and their feelings. How can you tell how a character feels? From what they say, do and think.
Characters are the people, animals or buddies in a story. We find out what they are like from what they say, do and think. Read Juno's story: what is Juno like?
Juno wanted the biggest buddy in the village. She built a giant from forty stone blocks. When she tapped it with her wand, it yawned, stretched and sat down on her roof.
The next morning, old Mr Pell came running. "My cat Pebble is stuck in the old mine! The tunnel is too narrow for me." Juno's giant tried to squeeze in, but only its nose would fit.
Juno looked at the last block in her bag: one small lantern. She built a buddy no bigger than a mug and woke it up. It glowed and blinked. "I'll call you Wick," she said.
Wick zipped into the dark tunnel, lighting the way. Soon Pebble came out, following the little glow, with Wick bouncing behind her. Mr Pell hugged his cat and laughed.
That night, the giant carried Wick on its shoulder to the village party. "Some jobs need someone big," it rumbled, "and some need someone small." Juno smiled.
The theme is the big idea a story teaches, like "friends help each other". Ask yourself: what did the characters learn? Juno learned that small can be just right. Next: reading to learn.

exercises.prompt: Who is the main character of the story?
exercises.hint: Who does the story follow from the start to the end?
exercises.explain: The story is about Juno from the first line to the last.

exercises.hint: Look at what Mr Pell said.
exercises.explain: Mr Pell said Pebble was stuck in the old mine.

exercises.prompt: Why could the giant buddy not help at first?
exercises.hint: What happened when it tried to squeeze in?
choices: It was too big for the tunnel
exercises.explain: Only its nose would fit: the tunnel was too narrow for it.

exercises.prompt: Wick was made from a lantern block.
exercises.hint: What was the last block in Juno's bag?
exercises.explain: Juno built Wick from her last block: one small lantern.

exercises.hint: What happened first? What did that lead to?
items: Wick lights the way into the tunnel.
Mr Pell's cat is stuck in the mine.
exercises.explain: Juno builds a giant, Pebble gets stuck, Juno builds Wick, and Wick lights the way.

exercises.prompt: Which word best describes Juno at the end of the story?
exercises.hint: She found a new way to help when her first plan did not work.
exercises.explain: Juno thought again and built the right buddy for the job: she was thoughtful.

exercises.prompt: Mr Pell could go into the tunnel himself.
exercises.hint: What did Mr Pell say about the tunnel?
exercises.explain: He said the tunnel was too narrow for him.

exercises.prompt: What did the giant do when it first woke up?
exercises.hint: Read the first part of the story again.
choices: It yawned and sat on Juno's roof
exercises.explain: It yawned, stretched and sat down on Juno's roof.

exercises.prompt: What is the theme of the story?
exercises.hint: What did Juno and the giant learn?
choices: Big or small, everyone has something to give
Giants are better than tiny buddies
Cats should stay out of mines
exercises.explain: Big or small, everyone has something to give: the giant and Wick each had their own job.

exercises.prompt: Why did Pebble come out of the tunnel?
exercises.hint: What did Wick do in the dark tunnel?
exercises.explain: Wick lit the way, and Pebble followed the little glow.

exercises.prompt: What did the giant mean: "some jobs need someone small"?
choices: Small buddies can do things big ones cannot
The giant wanted to be small
Every job is a small job
exercises.explain: Wick could go where the giant could not: small buddies can do things big ones cannot.

exercises.prompt: Juno tells this story herself, using "I".
exercises.hint: Look at how the story talks about Juno.
exercises.explain: The story says "Juno wanted…" and "she said": someone outside the story tells it.

exercises.prompt: How did Juno change from the start of the story to the end?
exercises.hint: What did Juno want at the start? What did she see at the end?
exercises.explain: At first Juno wanted the biggest buddy. By the end, she saw that her tiny buddy Wick could do what the giant could not.
choices: She saw that small buddies matter too
She grew afraid of the mine

exercises.prompt: Which detail from the story shows that Wick was brave?
exercises.hint: Which thing that Wick did could have been scary?
exercises.explain: Wick zipped into the dark tunnel all alone to find Pebble: that was brave.
choices: Wick zipped into the dark tunnel
Wick rode on the giant's shoulder

exercises.prompt: Match each character to who they are.
matches: a cat stuck in the mine
an old man in the village
exercises.hint: Think of what each one does in the story.
exercises.explain: Juno builds the buddies, Mr Pell is the old man who asks for help, Pebble is his cat, and Wick is the tiny lantern buddy.

exercises.prompt: Sort what each buddy did: the giant or Wick?
items: lit the way in the tunnel
carried a friend to the party
exercises.hint: Remember which buddy was big and which was small.
exercises.explain: The giant sat on the roof, got only its nose into the tunnel and carried Wick to the party. Wick glowed, blinked and lit the way.

exercises.prompt: Put the end of the story in order.
items: The giant carries Wick to the party.
exercises.hint: Ask what has to happen before Pebble can come out.
exercises.explain: Wick zips in, Pebble follows the glow out, Mr Pell hugs his cat, and that night the giant carries Wick to the party.

exercises.prompt: Match each clue to what it shows about a character.
exercises.hint: Ask what each action tells you: why would someone do that?
exercises.explain: Building again shows Juno did not give up. Zipping into the dark shows Wick was brave. Running shows Mr Pell was worried. Carrying Wick shows the giant was kind.

exercises.prompt: Sort the sentences: the theme, or only what happened?
items: Big or small, everyone can help.
Pebble got stuck in the mine.
exercises.hint: A theme is a big idea you could use in your own life, not one event.
exercises.explain: The theme is a lesson for anyone: everyone can help, and some jobs need someone small. Pebble getting stuck and Juno's giant are events in this one story.
